title: Dex's Wobbly Tower to Wonderful
markdown:
Dex and Biscuit were at the Big Library Bash, the most amazing event for inventors. This year: the Build-a-Contraption fair. Dex’s invention was meant to be the tallest, prettiest tower ever. Sparkly bits glued with glitter goo. Whirly bits that spun with a whizz-pop. A flag that went flappity-flap.

Every time they added just one more shimmery level — CRUMBLE-POP-WHIZZ! The tower tumbled. Biscuit let out a sad little Awwwoooo.

“Oh, fudgsicles!” Dex’s nose twitched. Biscuit, a furry ball of comfort, nudged his hand.

Dr Hale, head librarian, wrung her hands. Spectacles perched like a wise owl. “Dex, dear. Your contraption is quite wiggly. Like jelly doing a jig.”

He had tried fluffy clouds from a dream (they squished), bouncy springs (more wobble, super-jiggly jelly), and giant marshmallows (sticky, saggy, all over Biscuit’s tail). The tower still refused to stay up.

Dex flopped. Biscuit licked his cheek. Then his eyes found a display by the science books: a dinosaur skeleton, smooth white bony bits, all connected, standing STRAIGHT. Not a wobble. Strong. Together.

He padded over, Biscuit trotting behind. He ran a finger over a bone. It didn’t bend much. It wasn’t merely stiff. Cleverly built. A whole series of pieces working as one.

“Biscuit, look. These bits fit together. Little supports, and connectors too. Each piece helps the next stay up — and still lets it move.” He poked a rib. Sturdy. A leg bone: strong yet flexible. A quiet bony framework. Not a pile. A structure.

A grin arrived. “We’re just stacking! We need an inside skeleton!”

He scrambled back with a bounce. Smaller, sturdier plastic tubes and metal rods. An inside frame, like the dinosaur. Click! Clack! Snap! Biscuit’s tail wagged like a frantic metronome. Thump-thump-thump.

A flat sturdy cardboard base. More frame pieces upward, interlocking so they wouldn’t slip. Each piece a tiny bone for the ones above. Then the decorative bits and the flappity-flap flag, secured to the new strong framework.

It stood. Tall. Proud. Steady. No wobbles. No crumble-pops. Almost to the library’s high ceiling.

“Hooray!” Dex jumped. Biscuit yipped and did a spin-dance. Other inventors poked the tower, hunting a weak spot. There wasn’t one.

Dr Hale fluttered over, spectacles dancing. “So tall and un-wiggly! How did you do it?”

“Like the dinosaur. A frame inside, like bones. It holds everything up.”

She chuckled, warm as rustling pages. “The secret of the skeleton. Our own bodies have one: a framework that holds us up, protects the important insides, and lets us run, jump, and even do silly dances.” She tapped her leg. “Bones working together. Shape. And the chance to explore.”

Dex looked at the tower, the dinosaur, his own wiggling fingers. Hidden structures everywhere. A chair that didn’t wobble. A bouncy house that was perfectly bouncy. Biscuit wagged, ready.

Click! Clack! Snap! went nothing at all, because the tower had decided to stay. Thump-thump-thump went Biscuit, which was the sound of the next idea already arriving. WOOF!
characters: Dex (an invention tester), Biscuit (a dog), Hale (a scientist)
author: StoryGen Community
